text:
inc-bot: ALERT: 1837654321 - apac-west1 egress path showing elevated error-rate (5xx) for outgoing connections to partner peering. Auto-failover not triggered. Paging oncall SREs now. :rotating_light:
michelle: I'm on it. can someone grab customer impact? rough sketch: which customers in apac-west1 dedicated pools?
raj: pulling from inventory, give me 30s. looks like 3 dedicated pools + hosted traffic. 2 major customers with reserved capacity in apac-west1 (acme-ai, clearperch).
olivia: seeing spikes on the egress LB to peer ASNs — tcp resets + 503s from edge-egress-proxy. Logs: `EGRESS_ERROR rate=0.18 for prefix 203.0.113.0/24`
dante: adding context: yesterday we rolled an eBPF datapath change in apac-west1 for conn-tracking. rollback attempted?
michelle: don't roll anything yet. need to verify scope. if automated failover exists, why didn't it flip? check routing policy.
support-bot: Noted. Creating customer-notify drafts for impacted customers.
raj: quick grep: health-check service shows 2/5 egress nodes in apac-west1 unhealthy since 1837654000. autoscaler hasn't scaled up because nodes are flapping.
inc-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-APAC-W1-EGRESS. Severity: S2 (degraded). Commander: michelle. Runbook: egress-routing-failover-v2.
michelle: michelle: Handoff plan: I will coordinate mitigations, raj to own routing checks, olivia to gather metrics and logs, dante to validate kernel/db changes, james to prep status-page copy, naomi to handle customer comms for acme-ai.
michelle: Mitigation priority: 1) confirm scope 2) trigger manual regional reroute for hosted traffic 3) advise Dedicated customers on failover options 4) status page update
raj: routing check: `ip route show table egress-apac` shows fallback route present but next-hop health false. Running `ip route replace` to point to apac-west2 egress-bounce for hosted pool only. Patching now.```

michelle: please paste the exact command you ran for audit.
raj: pasted: ```bash
# redirect hosted pool outbound to apac-west2 egress
ip route replace 203.0.113.0/24 via 10.2.5.12 table egress-apac
ip rule add from 10.1.0.0/16 table egress-apac pref 100
```

olivia: Metrics update: request success rate for apac-west1 down from 99.9% -> 92% in last 6m. Latency up ~45ms for rerouted hosts. KV-cache hit unaffected. Sending dashboard snapshots.

dante: kernel change? the eBPF socket filter was showing segfaults on 2 nodes. I pushed a temporary unload on nodes node-12 and node-14. Haven't touched the rest.

michelle: good. keep that limited. we need a clear rollback if load shifts unexpectedly.

james: Status page draft (short): ```
We're investigating elevated outbound errors from apac-west1 affecting third-party peering and some hosted requests. We're routing hosted traffic to an alternate region (apac-west2) to reduce customer impact. Dedicated pools in apac-west1 may experience intermittent errors — we're contacting affected customers directly. Expected mitigation in >15min; next update in 30m or on resolution.```

michelle: tweak to call out customer-visible impact and what we're doing for dedicated customers. include contact for dedicated SLAs.

james: updated: ```
Incident: Egress degradation in apac-west1
Impact: Some hosted requests and a subset of Dedicated customers in apac-west1 are seeing increased 5xxs and higher latency. 
Action: We've rerouted hosted traffic to apac-west2 and are contacting Dedicated customers about manual failover and suggested traffic diversion. 
ETA: partial mitigation in ~15-20m. Contact: support@redwood.ai (for urgent SLA escalations use your account rep).```

naomi: customer template for acme-ai: ```
Hi Acme team —
We're investigating an infrastructure issue impacting outbound connections from apac-west1. You may see increased 5xxs from your dedicated pool. We're recommending a manual failover to apac-west2. If you'd like we can initiate the failover on your behalf (requires your approval). Expected restoration: 20-30 minutes. We'll update you via this thread and the status page. Apologies for the disruption. — Naomi, Customer Reliability
```

support-bot: Sent initial notify to acme-ai and clearperch (ticket IDs: SUP-9821, SUP-9822). Copy of message stored in ticket.
michelle: Good. Next: telemetry check for rerouted flows to apac-west2 to ensure no overload. olivia take that.
olivia: watching apac-west2 egress cpu and queue lengths. so far stable but one node showing queue length bump. autoscaling triggered one extra egress node.
raj: routing logs show ~40% of hosted flow successfully rerouted. Some clients still hitting apac-west1 because TTL on DNS entries. We're spinning up a DNS flush job for edge caches. Command: `kubectl exec -n edge cache-flusher -- /scripts/flush-caches --zone apac-west1`
michelle: schedule that and monitor. also prepare a rollback play if apac-west2 degrades. set `failover-stable` flag to true only after 10m of stable p95 latency.
inc-bot: NOTE: Oncall rotation change at 1837654680 - raj acknowledged, mike acknowledged.
michelle: On-call handoff: I'm staying as incident commander for now. If you need a break ping me and i'll pass baton. raj you're primary for routing.
dante: small pointer: for Dedicated customers we have per-customer iptables rules to avoid asymmetric routing hits. manual instructions: ```bash
# for dedicated pool fallback
sudo snat --to-source 198.51.100.10 -d 203.0.113.0/24
```
naomi: Acme replied: "Yes please failover us now" — they gave approval.
michelle: ok raj/dante coordinate to flip acme to apac-west2. naomi please confirm when done. raj/dante proceed.
raj: flipping acme pool now. command: `redwoodctl pool reroute --pool acme-ai-pool --region apac-west2 --force --reason "egress degradation apac-west1"`
olivia: telemetry: acme pool requests drop in 503s from 18% -> 3% after flip. latency up 30ms. hosted general error rate improving to 95% success across 10m window.
michelle: excellent. james update status page: note that acme accepted manual failover and we performed targeted pool reroutes.
james: status page updated. added note about manual failover and list of affected dedicated accounts (acme-ai, clearperch).
support-bot: Customer clearperch asked for guidance; advised manual failover playbook and offered assistance. awaiting reply.
michelle: timecheck: 24m since alert. current impact: partial; hosted mostly rerouted; dedicated: two accounts in progress. next update in 20m or sooner if status changes. I'm going to create a short internal post-incident checklist for root cause triage, keep replies inline here.
inc-bot: Reminder: attach incident timeline and logs to INC-2026-APAC-W1-EGRESS once resolved.
michelle: Closing notes for now: mitigate complete for hosted traffic, dedicated customers have manual rollback options and were notified. Root cause suspected eBPF conntrack regression — engineering followup assigned to dante + infra-ml team. I'll keep incident open until we have RCA and remediation plan. Thanks all. :heart:
